bull.t: Rapid revenue growth and high gross margin
bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion alongside very high gross margins indicates improving product economics as commercialization develops. If sales continue scaling, the margin profile could provide meaningful operating leverage and support reinvestment in marketing, distribution, and international expansion.

Repeat purchasing and encouraging annualized pack volumes provide evidence that VIZZ may generate recurring demand rather than only initial prescriptions. Stronger persistence can improve customer lifetime value, make commercial spending more productive, and support a more durable prescription base.

International partners and multiple regulatory submissions broaden the potential market beyond the United States while sharing commercialization responsibilities. Additional approvals and launches could diversify revenue sources and create longer-term licensing or product-sales opportunities.

bear.b: Substantial operating losses and negative cash generation mean the company has not yet converted commercialization into financial self-sufficiency. Continued spending at this level can consume available liquidity and increase reliance on external funding before the product reaches scale.

A major workforce reduction and CEO succession may lower the cost base, but they also create execution risk during a critical commercialization phase. Operational disruption, loss of organizational capacity, and interim leadership could hinder marketing, regulatory, and launch priorities.

bear.t: Weak retail adoption and uncertain recurring prescribing
bear.b: Limited retail traction reduces the breadth of distribution and makes demand less visible outside e-pharmacy channels. If professional awareness does not translate into repeat prescribing, patient acquisition may remain dependent on consumer-led channels and require sustained commercial spending.
